identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza presents this as an open-top alternative to its existing closed C3.R. A unique real-world referent is not established, so related FIA homologation evidence is used only for manual-gearbox context and exact controls come from the guided AMS2 test.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed-top round rim without integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights. Open-top describes the vehicle body, not the steering rim.

notes: The clutch is required to move from rest, but correctly rev-matched running shifts were accepted without it.
Full-throttle clutchless upshifts were rejected and succeeded only after a throttle lift; clutchless downshifts were rejected until the driver supplied a manual blip.
This is a separate record so the directly verified convertible technique is not silently applied to the older closed-car record.
Guided live test completed with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled.
Standing-start clutch, four direct H selections, required lift/manual blip, and the closed round rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: The exact AMS2 identity and complete user-facing controls were directly tested. Real-world identity remains explicitly uncertain rather than being inferred from the related homologation form.

claims.basis: Official Reiza context and exact live telemetry establish the distinct open-top game variant and class.
Related FIA evidence supports conventional manual H hardware, while direct AMS2 testing establishes the exact four-gear interface.
Guided current-game A/B tests directly established standing-start clutch, lift/manual-blip requirements, absence of automatic cut/blip, and wheel details.

archetype.basis: No registered archetype is a four-speed H-pattern that needs the blip. The registered four-speed leaves it optional, and this car requires it. Whether that is a departure or a different mechanism turns on gearbox_type, which is unestablished: dog rings need the driver to match revs, which would make these cars an archetype of their own rather than a variation on the synchromesh one. Six curated cars sit in exactly this position. A reviewed source settles all of them together.

notes: The unique real-world referent remains unknown; simulator behavior is exact and versioned.
